# dsh-hello

The smallest possible bundle: one row, no client half, no services, no state.

## Behaviour

Logs `[dsh-hello] loaded` once at boot and does nothing else.

Its job is to answer one question — *does this Harness installation load a linked local plugin at all?* — before you debug a real plugin. A host-only plugin exercises the patch row, the Loader import, and TypeScript source loading, and nothing more, so when it works the remaining variables are your plugin's.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/hello
```

If boot prints nothing, the row never mounted: start with `dsh --profile dev --dump-config` and check that `hello` is in the composed tree.

## Limits

It proves loading, not rendering. A client half is a different path — the bundle protocol, the slot registry, and the boot graph can all fail while this plugin stays quiet. For that, use a client plugin with a test that drives its bundle.

## Tests

None, by design. There is no logic to drive; the only assertion is the log line, which you read at boot.

# dsh-su

A monorepo of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins. The Harness itself is installed globally; this repo holds plugin sources only, and links them into a profile.

## Getting started

```sh
git clone https://github.com/serhaturtis/dsh-su && cd dsh-su
./setup.sh                             # Node, then the Harness, then the plugins
dsh --profile web web                  # boot the GUI
```

`./setup.sh` is a shell script for one reason: it may need to run *before Node
exists*, and `bootstrap.mjs` is a Node program. It uses an existing nvm to
provision Node 24 (see [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc)) if Node is missing, and
installs nvm — `curl … | bash`, a bigger decision than installing a CLI — only
when passed `--install-node`. Its one limitation is shell-shaped: a script
cannot change the PATH of the shell you are standing in, so if it installs nvm
it prints the two lines to add to your shell rc.

With Node already on PATH, `./setup.sh`, `pnpm setup`, and
`node scripts/bootstrap.mjs` are the same thing. `bootstrap` takes it from
there:

1. **installs the Harness** globally at the version pinned in `package.json`, if `dsh` is missing (`--no-harness-install` refuses and prints the command instead);
2. checks pnpm, which `dsh plugin` forwards to;
3. installs workspace dependencies;
4. **creates the profile from the shipped `web` template** if it doesn't exist;
5. links every plugin in the repo into it.

It never *upgrades* an installed Harness — a version mismatch is reported with the exact command, because a global upgrade mid-project is your call. Re-running is safe: it is the repair command as much as the setup one.

Flags: `--dry-run` reports without changing anything, `--profile <name>` targets another profile, `--no-install` skips workspace deps, `--no-harness-install` leaves the global Harness alone.

## Plugins

| Plugin | Shows up as | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`status-widget`](plugins/status-widget/README.md) | bottom-right card | Account balance and rate class cached 60s, eight-state cat mascot, [character packs](plugins/status-widget/docs/character-packs.md) |
| [`rate-hours`](plugins/rate-hours/README.md) | composer row | Peak/off-peak rate badge with a countdown; weekday schedule, public holidays not tracked |
| [`hello`](plugins/hello/README.md) | boot log | Smoke test that a linked plugin loads at all |

Add a row when you add a plugin. The table is the index; each plugin's README is the detail.

What is next, and what is deliberately parked, is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Layout

```
setup.sh                 shell entry point: provisions Node, then runs bootstrap
.nvmrc                   the Node version this repo is developed on
plugins/<name>/          one bundle per directory; <name> is the short name
  package.json           dsh.bundle.patch, dsh.client, exports
  cordis.patch.yml       the row this bundle inserts
  src/index.ts           host half: export name / inject / apply(ctx)
  src/client.js          client half (optional): a client-module bundle
  test/*.test.mjs        node tests, no Harness runtime
  README.md              behaviour, install, limits, tests
scripts/                 workspace tooling: bootstrap, sync, scaffold, test runner
docs/plugin-contract.md  what the Harness requires, and its sharp edges
ROADMAP.md               what is next, with effort and reasoning
```

## Conventions

- **Directory name is the short name; package name is `dsh-<short>`.** One plugin, one directory, one package, one row.
- **The exported Cordis `name` equals the package name**, so boot logs and the composed tree agree with the directory.
- **Every plugin has a README** with four sections, in order: behaviour, install, limits, tests. The limits section is not optional — it is where a plugin admits what it cannot know.
- **Tests are plain `node`,** no framework, no dependencies. `node scripts/test-all.mjs` (also `pnpm test`) finds `plugins/*/test/*.test.mjs` and runs each in its own process.
- **No build step** while plugins are plain JavaScript. A TypeScript client half would need one; nothing here has that yet.
- **`private: true` and `0.x`** until a plugin is worth publishing.
- **Two-space JSON/YAML/Markdown, tabs in source.**

Start a plugin with the scaffold rather than copying a neighbour:

```sh
pnpm new <name>            # host-only
pnpm new <name> --client   # host + browser half
```

## Dev loop

```sh
node scripts/new-plugin.mjs <name> --client   # scaffold a conforming plugin
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile dev   # link + enable it
pnpm dev                                      # boot the Web UI on the dev profile
```

`sync-profile` is the only step that touches a profile. It is idempotent — it links what's missing, adds the bundle row, and reports stale links left by deleted plugins (`--prune` removes them) — so run it after adding, renaming, or deleting a plugin instead of remembering `dsh plugin add` per package:

```sh
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --dry-run   # report, change nothing
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web             # apply
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --except rate-hours  # keep one out for good
```

- `bootstrap` is `sync-profile` plus the version checks and workspace install, i.e. the same thing for a machine that has never run this repo.
- A profile that doesn't exist yet is **seeded from the shipped `web` template** (`--template` changes that), so a fresh machine needs no manual profile creation. An existing profile that lacks `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` gets a warning with the repair command instead of being rewritten — seeding replaces profile-local settings, so that stays your call.
- Profiles live at `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>` (`~/.dsh` by default); `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` prints the composed tree without booting. `pnpm dev` uses the default port, so stop the running GUI first or pass `--port` to `dsh` directly.
- **Client code is composed at boot**: restart the Host after editing `src/client.js`. The Harness is a global install here, not a checkout, so there is no client HMR.
- Plugins are linked, so source edits need only a restart. Published plugins should ship built JS instead of raw `src/*.ts`.
- Bump the Harness with `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`, update `dsh.harness.version` in `package.json`, and re-read [`docs/plugin-contract.md`](docs/plugin-contract.md) — the bundle contract is version-sensitive.

## Verifying

```sh
node scripts/test-all.mjs                  # every plugin's suite; no install needed
dsh --profile dev --dump-config            # composition, no boot
pnpm sync --profile dev --dry-run          # what the profile is missing
```

`pnpm test` runs the same script, but pnpm re-checks the workspace install first — reach for the direct command when `node_modules` is stale or absent.

A throwaway Harness home keeps experiments out of `~/.dsh`:

```sh
DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-dev dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/<name>
```

`.dsh-dev/` is gitignored.

# dsh-rate-hours

> **Status: reference implementation, excluded from the `web` profile.** `status-widget` also shows the rate in the corner, so this composer-row badge is optional. It stays because it is the schedule implementation the parity test drives, and because a composer-row variant is a reasonable thing to re-enable with `sync-profile --include rate-hours`.

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that shows whether DeepSeek is billing you at **peak** or **off-peak** rates right now, and when that changes.

```
● Peak pricing · off-peak in 2h 30m
● Off-peak · peak in 13h 39m
● Weekend off-peak · peak in 1d 22h
```

It sits in the composer row (`conversation.input.left`), just before the model selector. Only the dot carries colour — the text inherits the theme — so it reads as part of the row rather than a widget on top of it.

| Dot | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| 🔴 Red | Peak — full rate |
| 🟡 Amber | Weekday off-peak — half rate |
| 🟢 Green | Off-peak all day (weekend) |

Hover for the schedule, the next boundary in UTC, and the caveats.

## The schedule

Peak is **01:00–04:00** and **06:00–10:00 UTC, Monday to Friday**. Everything else is off-peak — including weekends, and Chinese public holidays, which DeepSeek bills off-peak in full (this badge does not track those; see below). Off-peak is billed at half the peak rate.

Source: [DeepSeek Models & Pricing](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/quick_start/pricing).

Older write-ups describe a single `16:30–00:30 UTC` off-peak window. That is out of date; DeepSeek split peak into the two weekday blocks above.

### Chinese public holidays are not tracked

The badge runs the weekday rule year-round. DeepSeek's official holiday spans are republished by the State Council every year, and carrying that table was yearly maintenance with a bad failure mode: a late or forecast year could silently mis-price days. The table has been removed, so a holiday weekday shows as **peak** here even though the API bills it off-peak. The tooltip says so. On a holiday, check the pricing page before relying on the badge.

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/rate-hours   # from the repo root
```

That links the package into the profile and adds the `dsh-rate-hours` bundle. Restart the Host afterwards: the client-module graph is composed at boot, so a running page will not pick the plugin up.

The bundle is plain JavaScript served straight from `exports["./client"]`, so there is **no build step** — edit `src/client.js`, restart, reload.

## How it works

- **Host half** (`src/index.ts`) exists only to give the Loader a row: client bundles are discovered by scanning enabled Loader entries for a `dsh.client` declaration. It registers no service, no route, and no RPC.
- **Client half** (`src/client.js`) is a client-module bundle in the required shape: it calls `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory })` once and does everything else inside the factory closure. It requires only `react`, which is a platform seed module, so it declares no externals.
- **The clock is the browser's.** Computing locally avoids a Host round-trip, an RPC surface, and a route registration. The cost is that a badly skewed browser clock gives a wrong answer; the tooltip says the figure is browser-derived rather than presenting it as authoritative.

## Limits

- **An indicator, not a bill.** It reports the published schedule. It cannot know about account credits, negotiated discounts, or a schedule change DeepSeek makes without updating this file.
- **Chinese public holidays are not tracked.** A holiday weekday is shown as peak. The tooltip states the limitation; the table was removed rather than maintained by hand every year.
- **No cost estimate.** Deliberately out of scope; the session usage projection is a separate concern and a harder claim to make honestly.

## Tests

```sh
node test/schedule.test.mjs
```

The tests need no dependencies, so they run straight from a checkout. (`pnpm --filter dsh-rate-hours test` also works once the workspace has been installed; the plugin's only dependency is a `cordis` devDependency for editor typings, and `import type` is erased at runtime.)

22 checks, no Harness runtime needed: the loader handshake (bundle registers under the right id, exports `apply`/`inject` rather than a factory, registers into `conversation.input.left`), every peak edge, the gap between blocks, weekends, the public-holiday limitation, transition correctness across a full week, and the component's element tree.

The component is rendered against a React stub, not real React: the browser shell ships its own React bundle, so there is no React on disk for an SSR render in this workspace.

# rig-studio

A 2D skeletal animation runtime for DSH: characters as data — a rig (skeleton and anatomy), attachments (clothing, hair, tails, props), variants, and presets that select them.

Design: [`docs/design.md`](docs/design.md).

**Status:** M0 done, M1 core done — the pure engine plus the renderer (with a recording context) and the editor operations, 105 tests. Not yet wired into a canvas: client bundles cannot require relative modules, so that needs a small build step.

The whole design turns on two decisions that are easy to miss:

- **Attachments are overlays on one compiled skeleton.** Clothing is never baked into the body; attachment bones are merged at compile time, so FK, IK, springs and draw order are uniform, and a new piece of clothing costs one drawing, not a whole character. Facing is not the engine's business: an app maps its headings to views, and mirroring is one boolean.
- **Joints are covered by a disc centred on the pivot.** A circle is rotation-invariant, so a joint built this way cannot open a gap at any angle. Limits then become a style choice rather than a safety net.

Not in v1: mesh deformation, cloth collision, 8-direction art.

## Planned milestones

| # | Deliverable |
| --- | --- |
| M0 ✅ | format, compile, solver, clip sampling, IK, lint — every lint code has a test |
| M1 | canvas renderer and editor (bones, pivots, discs, scrub) |
| M2 | controller, blending, preset switching |
| M3 | two-bone IK and foot planting |
| M4 | spring bones for hair, tails, cloth |
| M5 | first character: humanoid, idle/walk/wave/squat |
| M6 | second preset, 8-direction data |
| M7 | quadruped sharing clips through bone roles |

```sh
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --except rate-hours  # keep one out for good
```

- `bootstrap` is `sync-profile` plus the version checks and workspace install, i.e. the same thing for a machine that has never run this repo.
- A profile that doesn't exist yet is **seeded from the shipped `web` template** (`--template` changes that), so a fresh machine needs no manual profile creation. An existing profile that lacks `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` gets a warning with the repair command instead of being rewritten — seeding replaces profile-local settings, so that stays your call.

- Plugins are linked, so source edits need only a restart. Published plugins should ship built JS instead of raw `src/*.ts`.
- Bump the Harness with `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`, update `dsh.harness.version` in `package.json`, and re-read [`docs/plugin-contract.md`](docs/plugin-contract.md) — the bundle contract is version-sensitive.

## Verifying

```sh

dsh --profile dev --dump-config            # composition, no boot
pnpm sync --profile dev --dry-run          # what the profile is missing
```


evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-status-widget

A speech bubble in the bottom-right corner, in which the **account balance** and the **DeepSeek rate class** appear as her dialogue — with a tail that points down at the character speaking them.

```
● ¥110.00 · Off-peak · peak in 13h 39m
```

She also **drifts slowly along a docked edge when left alone**, does something occasionally while quiet (stretches, taps the fuselage), **announces the peak boundary** the moment it flips, warns once an hour when the balance falls under your threshold, and **purrs if you pat her head** — press the top third rather than the body. Menu and dialogue text follow the browser language (English or Chinese); rate labels are still English.

While a turn runs, a thin bar under the bubble shows how full the context window is — green, amber at 70%, red at 90% — from the `contextPressure` projection. It hides itself when no provider has reported capacity, because an unknown window is not an empty one.

When a turn finishes, the bubble adds a third line: **`Last turn $0.0042`**. That is the delta between two readings of the `tokenUsage` projection — the four provider-reported buckets — priced with the published list rates at whatever rate class was in force. Off-peak is exactly half, and a test holds that relationship rather than hard-coding both columns.

Each finished turn also feeds **`Today $0.123`**, a running estimate for your local day kept in this browser's storage. It resets at local midnight. This is not account spend: it counts model tokens for turns this page watched, priced the same way as `Last turn`.

When a turn is blocked waiting for your approval, she leans in, the line becomes **"Waiting for your approval"**, the dot turns red and pulses, and a cue plays if sound is on. That signal comes from `uiSession.sessionStatus.pendingInteraction` — a push-based store, so it costs one subscription and no polling.

A black Norwegian Forest cat with a white mask stands under it, in one of eight drawings: **idle**, **happy** (a turn just finished), **busy** (a turn is running), **worried** (the balance read failed), **sleepy** (ten quiet minutes), **wave** (first sighting), **pat** (a head pat) and **party** (the balance went up). She bobs while idle, hops when happy and leans in while busy. **Drag her anywhere (the bubble comes along)** — she snaps to the nearer edge and flips to face into the page. Click her to collapse the card to the balance alone.

The art is raster, one PNG per state. There is no vector fallback: a second drawing of the same character drifts away from the generated one, and a missing image is better reported than silently replaced by a different animal.

Hover for the full picture: the schedule and its next boundary, the granted/topped-up split, and how fresh the reading is.

This is the feature set of the popular whale widget, built as an ordinary DSH plugin rather than a 22,000-line script injected into the page.

## Behaviour

- **Balance** comes from [`GET /user/balance`](https://api-docs.deepseek.com/api/get-user-balance), read by the host half with the key from the credential store and served to the browser as amounts only. The key never reaches the page. Amounts pass through as the decimal strings the API returns — no float arithmetic on money.
- **The reading is cached for 60 seconds** in the host, so a page left open for an hour costs one request per minute, and concurrent tabs share one read.
- **Failures are named, not blank**: `no API key`, or `balance ?` for a rejected key or a network problem, each explained in the tooltip. Polling continues once a minute, so a fixed key recovers without a reload.
- **The rate line** follows the same rule as [`rate-hours`](../rate-hours/README.md): peak `01:00–04:00` and `06:00–10:00` UTC, Monday–Friday. Chinese public holidays are **not tracked**; DeepSeek bills them off-peak, so a holiday weekday shows as peak here. The tooltip states that limitation.

The mascot — a cat in the corner that reacts to turns, rate changes and a low balance — is replaceable; the format is in [`docs/character-packs.md`](docs/character-packs.md).

## Install

```sh
node scripts/bootstrap.mjs      # links every plugin in the repo
```

or this plugin alone:

```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add ./plugins/status-widget
```

Needs `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` in the credential store — Settings → Models, or the environment when the Host starts.

### The artwork

Four drawings, one per state: `assets/mascot-{idle,happy,busy,worried}.png`, all 432×788. They come from a single generated 2×2 expression sheet, cut apart with **one shared canvas, one scale, and alignment on her stance** — the horizontal centroid of the lowest 12% of each figure. Centring on the bounding box was wrong: a raised arm moves the box centre, which left two poses looking off-centre by up to 25px.

`assets/mascot.png` is a byte copy of the idle drawing: it is the URL an already-cached page asks for, and the fallback for an unknown state.

The design is deliberately alluring — harness-style crop top, fishnets, thigh-highs, peace sign — and deliberately clothed. Nudity and see-through fabric are out of scope for this artwork, whatever the prompt. The host serves them at `/dsh-status-widget/mascot.png?state=<state>`, because a client bundle cannot require a relative asset and inlining ~300 KB of base64 would ride in every page load. Responses carry an ETag and revalidate, so a redrawn face is not pinned by a stale cache.

An inline SVG is the fallback: if the route 404s or the file is missing, the corner still has a character in four expressions instead of a hole. `test/character.test.mjs` pins the properties that matter — PNG signature, alpha channel, at least 2× display size, under 400 KB.

### Preferences

Size and position are stored in `$DSH_HOME/status-widget.json`, written by a `PUT /dsh-status-widget/prefs` route and read back on load. That is deliberate: the web GUI and the desktop client do not share `localStorage`, so browser-only state would disagree between them. `localStorage` remains the offline fallback.

The same choice is available in **Settings → Status widget**, which shares the widget's live size store rather than keeping a copy — pick a size there and the mascot changes immediately.

### Placement modes

| Mode | Anchor | Bubble |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Docked** | side edge + 32px margin, moving the whole frame | identical shape in every mode |
| **Free** | left/top where you dropped her | identical shape in every mode |

**Two invariants.**

1. She is always centred in the bubble.
2. The widget is one fixed-width frame (**220px, equal to the bubble's cap**). The character is centred in it, the bubble is centred on her, and docking *moves the frame*. Nothing inside reflows because of docking, so the bubble keeps one shape and she keeps one place in it. Because the frame equals the cap, the bubble can never stick out past the frame.

The frame is a constant rather than derived from the bubble's text on purpose: a layout that adapts to its content is what made her drift in the first place.

**Centring is done by the flow, never by transforms.** The frame is a flex column with `alignItems: center`, so the bubble and the character are centred by layout. This matters: the idle animation animates `transform`, and CSS animations outrank inline styles — centring with `translateX(-50%)` was being cancelled by the bob animation, which is what made her sit off-centre. The left-edge flip uses the standalone `scale` property for the same reason.

Dragging within 48px of a side docks; anywhere else is free. Both modes are persisted (host-side preferences, `localStorage` as the fallback) and both are repaired on resize rather than stranded off-screen.

The root element is exactly the character's box — the bubble is absolutely positioned around it. That is what makes the text unable to move her: the layout no longer depends on the bubble's width at all.

### Sound

Synthesised with WebAudio — two short tones, no audio files to ship or license. A chime when a turn finishes, a lower tone when the balance read fails. **Off until switched on**, in Settings or by preference; the choice is stored host-side with the rest.

### Cost, honestly

The figure covers **model tokens only**, priced at list rates for the model chosen in Settings (Flash by default). It cannot see account credits, negotiated discounts, retries billed elsewhere, or a mid-turn model switch. Cache writes are priced as ordinary input, because DeepSeek publishes a cache read discount but no separate write premium. A delta that goes negative — possible if compaction resets the fold — is clamped to zero rather than reported as a refund. `Today` is the sum of these same estimates, so it inherits every one of those limits.

## Limits

- **The balance is the account's, not the session's.** It says what is left, not what this conversation has cost.
- **No usage history beyond today.** The `Today` estimate keeps only the current local day; the whale derives full spend from session logs, which is a much larger claim than this widget makes.
- **One product assumption:** the credential is the DeepSeek API key. A profile signed in through the DeepSeek *account* provider has no `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY`, so the card says so instead of reading nothing.
- **The art is generated, not drawn to the grid.** Judge it at 180 px wide — the size it actually ships. The four states are one generation, so continuity between poses is only as good as the sheet was.
- **Chinese public holidays are not tracked.** The badge runs the weekday peak rule year-round. DeepSeek bills holidays off-peak, so a holiday weekday is shown as peak; the tooltip says so rather than shipping a table that needs a State Council notice every November.
- **`Today` is an estimate, not a bill.** It lives in this browser's storage, counts only turns the page watched, resets at local midnight, and two tabs watching one turn can each add it. It cannot see account credits, discounts, or turns that happened while the page was closed.
- **The schedule is duplicated** from `rate-hours` rather than imported: client bundles cannot require each other without a cross-plugin dependency, and either plugin should work alone. [`test/schedule-parity.test.mjs`](test/schedule-parity.test.mjs) drives both copies over every 15-minute sample of 2026-2027 and fails if they diverge.

## Feature catalogue

[`docs/feature-catalogue.md`](docs/feature-catalogue.md) lists **166 candidate features** with effort and value, drawn from the three DSH widgets plus Shimeji, Desktop Goose, Tamagotchi-style pets and VS Code Pets. 26 are shipped; the rest are scored and IDed (`E03`, `F07`, …) so commits and issues can reference them.

## Character packs

A standard for replacing the mascot: a directory (`pack.json` + images) or a single shareable `.dshchar` file, with the same manifest in both. Nobody's character art ships with this repository: the format is public, the art is personal. [`examples/README.md`](examples/README.md) walks through authoring one — the smallest valid pack, motion, and the mistakes that produce drifting or cropped frames.

Import, export, activate, delete and **Rescan** are live in Settings → Status widget → Character and over the host routes; the right-click Character submenu offers the same switch and import. The format, its refusals, the storage layout, routes, import/export and versioning rules are specified in [`docs/character-packs.md`](docs/character-packs.md); the rules themselves live in [`src/pack.js`](../src/pack.js) with 16 tests, deliberately free of Node and DOM so the format can be checked without a running Harness.

Packs may carry **animated characters** — an animated GIF/WebP, or a sprite sheet with `frames`/`fps` in horizontal, vertical or grid layout — and **their own sounds** per event (`done`, `error`, `alert`, `pat`), which win over the built-in cues. The renderer, the per-state routes and the Settings controls are implemented and tested end to end.

## Research

Which client-side signals a root-scope widget can read, and what they unlock: [`docs/client-data-sources.md`](docs/client-data-sources.md) — including the finding that pending approvals come from `sessionStatus.pendingInteraction`, not from the `permissions` projection.


What the three most-installed character widgets in this ecosystem actually ship, which of their features are worth copying, and which ones are a configuration product wearing a mascot: [`docs/widget-research.md`](docs/widget-research.md).

## Todo

Every known gap in this plugin — layout, dialogue, a11y, tests, packaging — is listed in [`TODO.md`](TODO.md), with the shipped items marked.

## Tests

```sh
node test/balance.test.mjs          # normalization, the request, the cache
node test/host.test.mjs             # route, missing key, throwing store
node test/client.test.mjs           # bundle handshake, slot, rendered tree
node test/interaction.test.mjs      # drag, click/pat, menu focus and submenus
node test/character.test.mjs        # four state drawings, placement maths
node test/pack.test.mjs             # character-pack format and refusals
node test/schedule-parity.test.mjs  # this widget's schedule == rate-hours'
```

No Harness runtime and no network: the balance fetch is injected, and the component renders against a React stub — the browser shell ships its own React, so there is none on disk here.

# dsh-su

A monorepo of [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) plugins. The Harness itself is installed globally; this repo holds plugin sources only, and links them into a profile.

## Getting started

```sh
git clone https://github.com/serhaturtis/dsh-su && cd dsh-su
./setup.sh                             # Node, then the Harness, then the plugins
dsh --profile web web                  # boot the GUI
```

`./setup.sh` is a shell script for one reason: it may need to run *before Node
exists*, and `bootstrap.mjs` is a Node program. It uses an existing nvm to
provision Node 24 (see [`.nvmrc`](.nvmrc)) if Node is missing, and
installs nvm — `curl … | bash`, a bigger decision than installing a CLI — only
when passed `--install-node`. Its one limitation is shell-shaped: a script
cannot change the PATH of the shell you are standing in, so if it installs nvm
it prints the two lines to add to your shell rc.

With Node already on PATH, `./setup.sh`, `pnpm setup`, and
`node scripts/bootstrap.mjs` are the same thing. `bootstrap` takes it from
there:

1. **installs the Harness** globally at the version pinned in `package.json`, if `dsh` is missing (`--no-harness-install` refuses and prints the command instead);
2. checks pnpm, which `dsh plugin` forwards to;
3. installs workspace dependencies;
4. **creates the profile from the shipped `web` template** if it doesn't exist;
5. links every plugin in the repo into it.

It never *upgrades* an installed Harness — a version mismatch is reported with the exact command, because a global upgrade mid-project is your call. Re-running is safe: it is the repair command as much as the setup one.

Flags: `--dry-run` reports without changing anything, `--profile <name>` targets another profile, `--no-install` skips workspace deps, `--no-harness-install` leaves the global Harness alone.

## Plugins

| Plugin | Shows up as | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| [`status-widget`](plugins/status-widget/README.md) | bottom-right card | Account balance and rate class cached 60s, eight-state cat mascot, [character packs](plugins/status-widget/docs/character-packs.md) |
| [`rate-hours`](plugins/rate-hours/README.md) | composer row | Peak/off-peak rate badge with a countdown; weekday schedule, public holidays not tracked |
| [`hello`](plugins/hello/README.md) | boot log | Smoke test that a linked plugin loads at all |

Add a row when you add a plugin. The table is the index; each plugin's README is the detail.

What is next, and what is deliberately parked, is in [ROADMAP.md](ROADMAP.md).

## Layout

```
setup.sh                 shell entry point: provisions Node, then runs bootstrap
.nvmrc                   the Node version this repo is developed on
plugins/<name>/          one bundle per directory; <name> is the short name
  package.json           dsh.bundle.patch, dsh.client, exports
  cordis.patch.yml       the row this bundle inserts
  src/index.ts           host half: export name / inject / apply(ctx)
  src/client.js          client half (optional): a client-module bundle
  test/*.test.mjs        node tests, no Harness runtime
  README.md              behaviour, install, limits, tests
scripts/                 workspace tooling: bootstrap, sync, scaffold, test runner
docs/plugin-contract.md  what the Harness requires, and its sharp edges
ROADMAP.md               what is next, with effort and reasoning
```

## Conventions

- **Directory name is the short name; package name is `dsh-<short>`.** One plugin, one directory, one package, one row.
- **The exported Cordis `name` equals the package name**, so boot logs and the composed tree agree with the directory.
- **Every plugin has a README** with four sections, in order: behaviour, install, limits, tests. The limits section is not optional — it is where a plugin admits what it cannot know.
- **Tests are plain `node`,** no framework, no dependencies. `node scripts/test-all.mjs` (also `pnpm test`) finds `plugins/*/test/*.test.mjs` and runs each in its own process.
- **No build step** while plugins are plain JavaScript. A TypeScript client half would need one; nothing here has that yet.
- **`private: true` and `0.x`** until a plugin is worth publishing.
- **Two-space JSON/YAML/Markdown, tabs in source.**

Start a plugin with the scaffold rather than copying a neighbour:

```sh
pnpm new <name>            # host-only
pnpm new <name> --client   # host + browser half
```

## Dev loop

```sh
node scripts/new-plugin.mjs <name> --client   # scaffold a conforming plugin
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile dev   # link + enable it
pnpm dev                                      # boot the Web UI on the dev profile
```

`sync-profile` is the only step that touches a profile. It is idempotent — it links what's missing, adds the bundle row, and reports stale links left by deleted plugins (`--prune` removes them) — so run it after adding, renaming, or deleting a plugin instead of remembering `dsh plugin add` per package:

```sh
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --dry-run   # report, change nothing
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web             # apply
node scripts/sync-profile.mjs --profile web --except rate-hours  # keep one out for good
```

- `bootstrap` is `sync-profile` plus the version checks and workspace install, i.e. the same thing for a machine that has never run this repo.
- A profile that doesn't exist yet is **seeded from the shipped `web` template** (`--template` changes that), so a fresh machine needs no manual profile creation. An existing profile that lacks `@deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app` gets a warning with the repair command instead of being rewritten — seeding replaces profile-local settings, so that stays your call.
- Profiles live at `$DSH_HOME/profiles/<name>` (`~/.dsh` by default); `dsh --profile <name> --dump-config` prints the composed tree without booting. `pnpm dev` uses the default port, so stop the running GUI first or pass `--port` to `dsh` directly.
- **Client code is composed at boot**: restart the Host after editing `src/client.js`. The Harness is a global install here, not a checkout, so there is no client HMR.
- Plugins are linked, so source edits need only a restart. Published plugins should ship built JS instead of raw `src/*.ts`.
- Bump the Harness with `npm i -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>`, update `dsh.harness.version` in `package.json`, and re-read [`docs/plugin-contract.md`](docs/plugin-contract.md) — the bundle contract is version-sensitive.

## Verifying

```sh
node scripts/test-all.mjs                  # every plugin's suite; no install needed
dsh --profile dev --dump-config            # composition, no boot
pnpm sync --profile dev --dry-run          # what the profile is missing
```

`pnpm test` runs the same script, but pnpm re-checks the workspace install first — reach for the direct command when `node_modules` is stale or absent.

A throwaway Harness home keeps experiments out of `~/.dsh`:

```sh
DSH_HOME=$PWD/.dsh-dev dsh plugin --profile dev add ./plugins/<name>
```

`.dsh-dev/` is gitignored.

# dsh-dkitchen

[![Tests](https://github.com/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin/actions/workflows/tests.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin/actions/workflows/tests.yml)
[![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin)](https://github.com/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin/releases/latest)
[![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin)](LICENSE)

**English** | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md)

A DeepSeek Harness plugin that turns a repository into a kitchen: stations, tickets, long
jobs, and the bell that wakes a session when its job finishes.

Installing the bundle is the whole installation. The tools are registered inside the harness
process through `ctx.tools`, so there is no package to install, no separate profile to boot, no
broker to start, and no MCP server to spawn. Nothing else needs running.

> **Based on [917Dhj/dkitchen](https://github.com/917Dhj/dkitchen).** The kitchen itself — the
> stations, the ticket workflow, the house rules, and the bell that wakes a session — is the
> design of [917Dhj/dkitchen](https://github.com/917Dhj/dkitchen), and this plugin is its port
> to the DeepSeek Harness plugin runtime. See [Acknowledgements](#acknowledgements).

## Install

**From Discover.** In the harness, open **Plugins → Discover**, add this index

```text
https://raw.githubusercontent.com/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin/main/docs/market/index.json
```

and install `dkitchen`. The index pins an exact commit of this repository, so what you get is
what a release names.

**From a release.** Download the source archive of a tag from
[Releases](https://github.com/songmingjun3/dsh-kitchen-plugin/releases), then point
**Plugins → install bundle** at the unpacked directory.

Either way the harness composes `cordis.patch.yml` into the profile and loads `index.js`.
Restart the harness if it does not pick the bundle up by itself. On first start the bundle also
installs the setup skill into the machine-wide skill root, so `/setup-dkitchen` works in every
project.

A bundle that fails to register a tool does so silently — the process keeps running and the
tool simply is not there. Set `debug: true` in `cordis.patch.yml` to have each registration
reported on stderr.

## What it gives a session

| Group | Tools |
| --- | --- |
| Sessions | `dkitchen_new_session`, `dkitchen_send`, `dkitchen_read`, `dkitchen_info`, `dkitchen_rename`, `dkitchen_list_sessions`, `dkitchen_board`, `dkitchen_session_status` |
| Long jobs | `dkitchen_launch`, `dkitchen_logs`, `dkitchen_stop`, `dkitchen_run_status` |
| Tickets | `dkitchen_relay`, `dkitchen_merge`, `dkitchen_log`, `dkitchen_executor_status` |
| Watching | `dkitchen_watch`, `dkitchen_watch_state` |
| Configuration | `dkitchen_config`, `dkitchen_check_refs`, `dkitchen_status` |

The ticket tools need the `gh` CLI. Without it they say so and the rest keep working.

## How a repository configures its kitchen

Each call resolves `.dkitchen.toml` from the repository the session works in, never from the
directory the harness happened to start in — one harness process serves many repositories.

```toml
repo = "owner/name"

[kitchen]
stations = ["orchestrator", "designer", "verifier", "executor"]

[harness]
default_provider = "trae"
default_model = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"

[models.executor]
model = "deepseek-v4.1-flash"

[approval]
allow = ["dkitchen_*"]
```

`dkitchen_status` reports what one repository resolved, and `rootSource` says how that
repository was chosen: `argument`, `session`, or `process`. A `process` answer means the
repository was guessed rather than known.

## Two deliberate behaviours

**`[approval]` answers by rule, and defers by default.** The harness already asks the user
through its own panel, so a plugin that answered ahead of it would remove that decision.
Naming a tool under `allow` answers it without asking, which is what makes an unattended
kitchen able to run what it was configured for; anything else calls `next()`. With no
`[approval]` section the plugin changes no permission behaviour at all.

**A background job's settlement arrives as a session notice.** `ctx.jobs` announces it, so a
session that launched work does not have to poll.

## The page this bundle adds

`client.js` adds a section to this bundle's page in **Plugins**. It reports whether the bundle
is installed and enabled, and says where a repository's configuration lives. It has no
buttons, because nothing here needs running.

## Layout

| Path | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `index.js` | Mounting the plugin: injected services, per-call config resolution, tool registration |
| `lib/` | The tools and the rules behind them |
| `kitchen/` | The station rules the setup skill renders into a repository |
| `skills/setup-dkitchen/` | The setup skill, with a renderer that needs only Node |
| `scripts/market.mjs` | Generating and validating `docs/market/index.json` |
| `docs/plugin.md` | The user-facing guide: installing, every tool, every `.dkitchen.toml` key |
| `tests/` | The suite: `node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"` |

This repository is the bundle: `package.json`, `index.js`, and `lib/` are at the root, which is
why the market index names it without a `path`.

## Development

```bash
node --test "tests/*.test.mjs"     # the suite; nothing to install first
node scripts/market.mjs index --check
```

On Windows under a restricted shell, `node --test` cannot spawn its per-file child processes;
run `node --test --experimental-test-isolation=none "tests/*.test.mjs"` there instead.

Releasing: bump `version` in `package.json`, then push a matching tag such as `v1.0.0`. The
release workflow checks the two agree, runs the suite, regenerates the market index for that
tag's commit, and publishes the GitHub release.

## Acknowledgements

This plugin is a port, not an original design. The kitchen it implements — stations with fixed
duties, work handed off through GitHub issues as tickets, the status block every comment opens
with, the rules for when a station must stop and ask, and the bell that wakes a session when its
long job exits — comes from **[917Dhj/dkitchen](https://github.com/917Dhj/dkitchen)**, and this
repository follows its functional design closely on purpose: the vocabulary, the refusals, and
the order in which the orchestrator does things are all meant to match. Thank you to
917Dhj/dkitchen for thinking it through and writing it down.

What differs here is the runtime, not the kitchen. That project drove DeepSeek Harness sessions
from outside the process — a CLI, a broker, an MCP server, a separate profile. This one
registers the same tools inside the harness through `ctx.tools`, so installing the bundle is the
whole installation. The behaviour is meant to stay the same; where this port had to choose, the
choice is recorded in the commit that made it and in the tests.

The metaphor, and much of the workflow, traces further back: the Michelin-kitchen way of running
agents comes from Lauren Tan ([Poteto](https://github.com/poteto)), and the practice of keeping
tickets on GitHub issues started from the issue tracker setup in
[Matt Pocock's skills](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills).

## License

[MIT](LICENSE)

# dsh-balance-panel

> Fork of wenzetan/dsh-quota-panel, maintained at sunshaobei/dsh-balance-panel (npm: @sunshaobei/dsh-balance-panel). Renamed to avoid confusion with upstream.
# dsh-quota-panel

English | [中文](README.zh.md)

**dsh-quota-panel** is a **provider quota / balance status widget** for the
DeepSeek Harness (DSH) **web surface** (`dsh web`). It sits in the
bottom-right corner of the product UI, watches every AI provider whose API
key you have configured, and tells you at a glance how much balance /
quota is left — DeepSeek, OpenRouter, SiliconFlow, Moonshot, StepFun,
xAI, Zhipu GLM, OpenCode Go, Volcengine Ark (Agent/Coding Plan), plus one-api / new-api style aggregators,
and the **coding plans** (智谱 GLM Coding, Z.AI, Kimi Coding, MiniMax
Coding global/CN) with 5-hour / weekly usage windows and MCP monthly quota.
xAI, Zhipu GLM, OpenCode Go, **ChatGPT subscription (Plus/Pro via Codex
login)**, plus one-api / new-api style aggregators, and the **coding
plans** (智谱 GLM Coding, Z.AI, Kimi Coding, MiniMax Coding global/CN)
with 5-hour / weekly usage windows and MCP monthly quota.

Since v0.5 it is a **dual-face plugin** with a **built-in provider catalog
and auto discovery**: install it, restart `dsh web`, and every provider
whose key resolves automatically appears on the panel — zero configuration.
It needs **no npm dependencies** and asks for **no `allowBuilds` authorization**.

## Screenshots (real browser rendering)

Collapsed capsule, light theme:

![capsule (light)](docs/screenshot-light.png)

Expanded card, light theme:

![expanded (light)](docs/screenshot-light-expanded.png)

Settings panel (⚙), light theme:

![settings (light)](docs/screenshot-light-settings.png)

Collapsed capsule, dark theme:

![capsule (dark)](docs/screenshot-dark.png)

Expanded card, dark theme:

![expanded (dark)](docs/screenshot-dark-expanded.png)

Settings panel (⚙), dark theme:

![settings (dark)](docs/screenshot-dark-settings.png)

## Supported features

- **Auto discovery** — the host half ships a catalog of well-known
  providers; each entry names the provider's standard credential
  references, and **every provider whose key resolves
  (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` / `.env` / environment variables)
  appears on the panel automatically**, with zero config. Remove the key
  and the row disappears. No credential enumeration API exists in DSH, so
  the catalog is probed each refresh cycle.
- **Coding-plan usage windows** — GLM / Z.AI / Kimi / MiniMax coding
  plans render as usage rows: 5-hour window, weekly pool and (GLM/Z.AI)
  the MCP monthly lane, each with its own reset countdown; windows the
  plan does not carry show `—` instead of a fabricated 0%.
- **Two sizes** — collapsed: a minimal capsule with one independent
  "status dot + value" pair per account (`● ¥58.36 · ● 45%`); expanded: a
  full card with a row per provider (status dot, name, primary value,
  secondary info, progress bar for usage-kind providers).
- **Auto refresh** — follows the configured interval (default 60 s), paused
  while the page is hidden; the refresh button spins during a fetch and
  repeated clicks never fire concurrent requests.
- **Per-account status** — balance rows are graded by tier
  (`critical <= warn <= healthy`), usage rows by percent
  (`error >= warn`); the offending dot/value alone recolors, others stay
  calm. Usage percentages use battery-style three-color grading, independent
  of the status dots.
- **Settings panel (⚙)** — per-provider visibility, refresh interval,
  per-provider warning thresholds, per-provider **HTTP(S) proxy URL**, the
  **capsule display mode** (auto = highest window — the default — / 5h
  window / weekly window / highest), and "restore defaults". All local
  settings apply immediately, persist to browser localStorage, and are
  never written to the profile or uploaded.
- **Per-row HTTP(S) proxy** — configure a proxy for providers that cannot
  be reached directly from your network (see below).
- **One-api / new-api aggregators** — the built-in `openai-billing`
  format adapts aggregator dashboards.
- **Theming** — driven entirely by Harness design tokens
  (`--dsw-alias-*`, `--dsw-static-*`, `--dsw-shadow-*`,
  `--dsw-font-*`) with sensible fallbacks, so it follows the product
  theme (light/dark) and ships no palette of its own.
- **Security by construction** — API keys never reach the browser; the
  browser talks only to a loopback-only RPC channel and receives only
  normalized views (see "How it works").

## Not supported (yet)

- **Usage-only providers** — OpenAI, Anthropic, Together, Groq, Mistral,
  Cohere, DashScope, Baichuan expose no public "remaining balance"
  endpoint, only usage/cost queries (usually admin keys + time windows,
  "spent" semantics rather than "remaining"). Planned as a separate
  usage row kind showing monthly spend (Anthropic Admin API and OpenAI
  usage API first).
- **Cookie / CLI-only coding plans** — the quota pages of Qwen Token Plan
  (Bailian console), Xiaomi MiMo Token Plan, and Qoder expose no API-key
  quota endpoint: they require web cookies, the `arkcli` CLI, or chat-endpoint
  rate-limit probes (per
  [CodexBar](https://github.com/steipete/CodexBar/tree/main/docs) research).
  Volcengine Ark / Doubao Agent Plan and Coding Plan are now supported via
  the AK/SK-signed OpenAPI (see the catalog table above). Other providers on
  this list cannot be wired in until an API-key endpoint appears.
- **socks5 proxies** — only HTTP/HTTPS proxies are accepted (a socks URL
  is rejected with a clear per-row error).
- **Custom adapters** — new upstream formats cannot be plugged in from the
  profile; a `format` value outside the built-in set fails loud at mount.
- **Multi-page placements** — the widget lives in the `shell.overlay`
  slot only (bottom-right corner), not in sidebars, headers, or the status
  bar.

### Requesting a new provider

Missing a provider? [Open an issue](https://github.com/wenzetan/dsh-quota-panel/issues/new)
with:

1. **the provider id** you want (`^[a-z0-9-]+$`, e.g. `together`), using a
   `-cn` suffix for the China site of a dual-site provider
   (cf. `siliconflow` / `siliconflow-cn`);
2. **the balance API URL** — a public endpoint that answers the provider's
   standard API key with remaining balance/quota (e.g.
   `GET https://api.provider.com/v1/user/info`, Bearer auth), plus the
   response shape if you can paste it.

That is all the catalog needs: an id whose standard credential reference
resolves, an endpoint, and a format adapter for the response. Providers with
only cookie/CLI quota pages (see above) cannot be supported until they expose
an API-key endpoint.

## How it works

```
┌─────────────── browser (lib/client.js) ───────────────┐
│  shell.overlay slot → capsule / card / settings panel  │
│  localStorage: visibility · interval · thresholds ·    │
│                proxy URLs (frontend settings)          │
└──────────────┬─────────────────────────────────────────┘
               │ loopback-only Connection RPC: /dsh-quota-panel
               │   specs (render hints, no credentials)
               │   fetch-all { proxy: {rowId: url} } → normalized views
┌──────────────▼────────────── host (lib/index.js) ──────┐
│  ctx.credentials → API keys (never leave the host)      │
│  catalog probe → auto discovery (15 built-in providers) │
│  per-row fetch → proxy engine (CONNECT tunnel /         │
│                  absolute-URI) → upstream JSON          │
│  normalization → {balance | usage | info} view models   │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

- **Host half** (`lib/index.js`) registers one loopback-only Connection
  RPC channel `/dsh-quota-panel` with two endpoints:
  - `specs` — the resolved rows with render hints only (id, label, row
    kind, currency, threshold tiers, window labels, configured proxy name).
    No credentials, no endpoints.
  - `fetch-all` — fetches every visible row, normalizes each upstream
    response into a **generic view model** (`balance` / `usage` /
    `info`), and returns `{rows: [{id, view} | {id, error}], fetchedAt}`.
    Raw upstream JSON stays host-side like the keys; one failing row never
    affects the others.
- **Auto discovery** — because DSH's credential store has no enumeration
  API, the host half probes the catalog entries' standard refs each fetch
  cycle; every entry whose key resolves joins the panel, and entries with
  unresolvable keys are skipped (a missing key yields a clear per-row error
  only when it was explicitly configured via `providers`).
- **Proxy engine** — zero-dependency hand-rolled `proxiedGetJson`:
  https targets go through an HTTP `CONNECT` tunnel (TLS over the
  tunnel), http targets via absolute-URI forwarding. 15 s per-row timeout,
  1 MB body cap. Proxy selection precedence:
  **frontend settings panel > profile config > direct**.
- **Threshold judgement happens client-side** from the `specs` hints, so
  local threshold overrides apply without refetching; profile thresholds
  ship in `specs` and the frontend settings override them locally.
- **Config validation** — the exported `Config` schema (vendored
  schemastery) declares structure and defaults; cross-field constraints (id
  uniqueness, `critical <= warn <= healthy`, proxy references, catalog
  override keys) are validated host-side at mount and fail loud.
- **DOM safety** — the card builds DOM exclusively with
  `createElement`/`textContent`; API values never touch `innerHTML`;
  technical errors (401, timeout, missing credential, refused proxy) surface
  only in `title` tooltips or inline row text.

## Configuration

**Out of the box: nothing.** Install, restart, and any provider whose key
resolves appears automatically. The table below is only for tuning.

All keys are optional — the structure and defaults live in the exported
`Config` schema, so profile patches may omit every defaulted field.

| Key | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `auto` | probe the built-in catalog; providers with a resolvable key join the panel | `true` |
| `hide` | row ids to drop (catalog and explicit rows alike) | `[]` |
| `proxies` | named proxy definitions `{<name>: "http://host:port"}`, HTTP(S) only | `{}` |
| `catalog` | partial overrides for auto-discovered rows `{<catalog-id>: {...}}` | `{}` |
| `refreshMs` | auto-refresh interval | 60000 |
| `providers` | explicit rows; a same-id entry replaces the catalog row wholesale | `[]` |

Each `catalog` override may set: `label` / `endpoint` / `format` /
`proxy` / `refs` (credential references to probe, UPPER_SNAKE) /
`secretRefs` (a second credential reference — required for the Volcengine
AK/SK pair; the row is only discovered when BOTH `refs` and `secretRefs`
resolve) / `region` (Volcengine OpenAPI region; default `cn-beijing`) /
`currency` (balance rows: symbol like `$` or `US$`) / `balanceTiers` /
`warnPercent` / `errorPercent` / `windowLabels`.

Explicit `providers` fields:

| Field | Meaning | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | row id (RPC rows align by id), `^[a-z0-9-]+$` | required |
| `label` | provider name shown on the card | required |
| `credential` | credential reference (`$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` or environment) | required |
| `secretCredential` | second credential reference (Volcengine `volcengine-agent-usage` / `volcengine-coding-usage`: the SK) | — |
| `endpoint` | quota JSON endpoint; base URL for `openai-billing` | required |
| `format` | row adapter (see table below) | `deepseek-balance` |
| `proxy` | a proxy name defined in `proxies`; absent = direct | — |
| `region` | (`volcengine-agent-usage` / `volcengine-coding-usage`) Volcengine OpenAPI region | `cn-beijing` |
| `currency` | (balance rows) currency symbol, overrides the format default | format default |
| `balanceTiers` | (balance rows) `{critical, warn, healthy}` | `{10, 20, 50}` |
| `lowBalance` | legacy alias for `balanceTiers.warn` | — |
| `windowLabels` | (usage-kind formats) labels for the usage windows | `{滚, 周, 月}` |
| `warnPercent` / `errorPercent` | (usage rows) thresholds | 70 / 90 |

### Built-in provider catalog (auto discovery)

| Provider | Credential refs probed | Endpoint | Row kind |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek | `DEEPSEEK_API_KEY` | `api.deepseek.com/user/balance` | ¥ balance |
| OpenRouter | `OPENROUTER_API_KEY` | `openrouter.ai/api/v1/credits` | $ balance (purchased − used) |
| SiliconFlow (global) | `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` | `api.siliconflow.com/v1/user/info` | $ balance |
| SiliconFlow (CN) | `SILICONFLOW_CN_API_KEY` | `api.siliconflow.cn/v1/user/info` | ¥ balance |
| Moonshot / Kimi | `MOONSHOT_API_KEY` | `api.moonshot.cn/v1/users/me/balance` | ¥ balance |
| MiniMax Coding (global) | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` | `www.minimax.io/v1/token_plan/remains` | 5h prompt usage % |
| MiniMax Coding (CN) | `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY` | `api.minimaxi.com/v1/token_plan/remains` | 5h prompt usage % |
| StepFun | `STEP_API_KEY` / `STEPFUN_API_KEY` | `api.stepfun.com/v1/accounts` | ¥ balance (hover: cash/voucher) |
| xAI | `XAI_API_KEY` | `api.x.ai/v1/billing/credits` | $ balance |
| Zhipu GLM | `ZHIPU_API_KEY` / `GLM_API_KEY` | `open.bigmodel.cn/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` | text row (quota remaining/total; no public balance API) |
| 智谱 GLM Coding | `ZAI_CODING_CN_API_KEY` | `open.bigmodel.cn/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` | coding-plan windows (5h tokens / weekly / searches) |
| Z.AI GLM Coding | `ZAI_API_KEY` | `api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` | coding-plan windows (5h tokens / weekly / searches) |
| Kimi Coding | `KIMI_API_KEY` | `api.kimi.com/coding/v1/usages` | usage % (5h rate limit + weekly request pool) |
| OpenCode Go | `OPENCODE_GO_API_KEY` | `opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage` | three-window usage % |
| Volcengine Ark Agent Plan | `VOLC_ACCESS_KEY` + `VOLC_SECRET_KEY` | `open.volcengineapi.com` (OpenAPI, signed) | usage % (5h / weekly / monthly, `GetAFPUsage`) |
| Volcengine Ark Coding Plan | `VOLC_ACCESS_KEY` + `VOLC_SECRET_KEY` | `open.volcengineapi.com` (OpenAPI, signed) | usage % (session / weekly / monthly, `GetCodingPlanUsage`) |

> Volcengine Ark has **two separate subscriptions — Agent Plan and Coding Plan** —
> shown as **two independent rows** (like two providers) that share the same
> AK/SK pair. Each row queries only its own plan's API and never falls back to
> the other, so a plan the account has not subscribed to shows a "not
> subscribed" message on that row instead of the other plan's numbers.
> Volcengine authenticates with an **AccessKey ID / SecretAccessKey pair** using
> HMAC-SHA256 request signing — not a Bearer token. The inference `ARK_API_KEY`
> (shaped `ark-...`) cannot query usage; only the AK/SK pair has OpenAPI
> permission. Full setup is in the next section.

#### Volcengine Ark setup

Ark Agent Plan / Coding Plan usage comes from the **control-plane OpenAPI**,
which requires an AK/SK pair with read-only access. Three steps:

**1. Create an AccessKey**

Open [https://console.volcengine.com/iam/keymanage](https://console.volcengine.com/iam/keymanage)
(Volcengine console → Identity and Access Management → Access Keys) and click
*New access key*. Prefer creating a **sub-user key** dedicated to this plugin
rather than using the primary account key. Save the AccessKey ID and
SecretAccessKey when shown — the SecretAccessKey is displayed once.

**2. Grant Ark read-only permission**

Attach the `ArkReadOnlyAccess` policy to the sub-user (or role) that owns the
key:

- Open [IAM → Users](https://console.volcengine.com/iam/user/list), pick the
  sub-user, choose *Permissions* → *Add permissions*;
- In the *Search policy name and remarks* box, type `ArkReadOnlyAccess`;
- The result whose **service source is "Volcengine Ark"** is the one you need — check it. There are only two same-named policies in the search results, and checking both is harmless too.

`ArkReadOnlyAccess` alone is sufficient — `GetAFPUsage` and
`GetCodingPlanUsage` are read-only actions; `ArkFullAccess` or account-level
billing permissions are not required.

**3. Save the credentials**

Add two lines to `$DSH_HOME/.credentials.yaml` (by default
`C:\Users\<you>\.dsh\.credentials.yaml` on Windows or `~/.dsh/.credentials.yaml`
on Linux/macOS):

```yaml
VOLC_ACCESS_KEY: AKLTxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
VOLC_SECRET_KEY: xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx
```

You can also use the `VOLC_ACCESS_KEY` / `VOLC_SECRET_KEY` environment
variables (DSH's credential resolver falls back to the environment). Restart
`dsh web`; the "Volcengine Agent" and "Volcengine Coding" rows appear in the
bottom-right panel automatically (whichever plan the account subscribes to
shows data; both rows share the same AK/SK pair) — no `providers:` block required.

**Verifying permissions**

After restart, check the panel:

- The Agent row shows three percentages (5h / weekly / monthly) and the Coding
  row shows three (session / weekly / monthly) → AK/SK and `ArkReadOnlyAccess`
  are both working (if only one plan is subscribed, the other row shows a
  "not subscribed" message);
- `volcengine SignatureDoesNotMatch: ...` → the SK was copied wrong (watch the
  trailing `=`);
- `volcengine AccessDenied: ...` → the policy is not attached or the wrong
  source policy was selected;
- `No active Volcengine Ark Agent/Coding Plan subscription` → the signature
  worked but the account has no subscription to that plan (typical for
  pay-as-you-go accounts; the two rows report independently — hide the
  unsubscribed one from the ⚙ settings panel).

> **Migration (from ≤ 0.9.1, if you pinned the old row):** the single
> catalog row id `volcengine` and the format id `volcengine-usage` were
> replaced by `volcengine-agent` (`volcengine-agent-usage`) and
> `volcengine-coding` (`volcengine-coding-usage`). Auto-discovered setups need
> no changes; a hand-written `catalog:` override or `providers:` entry that
> still references the old ids makes the plugin refuse to load with a
> validation error listing the valid ids — update it to the two new ids.

> Security note: an AK/SK pair can read all Ark usage data for the account.
> Redact it before pasting into chats, tickets, or screenshots, and rotate it
> from the [key management page](https://console.volcengine.com/iam/keymanage)
> when no longer needed.
| ChatGPT subscription (Plus/Pro) | in-plugin login or `~/.codex/auth.json` (no API key) | `chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage` | weekly usage % (Pro includes a 5h window) |

An additional **`openai-billing`** format adapts one-api / new-api style
aggregators: set `endpoint` to the aggregator base URL and the host half
requests `{base}/v1/dashboard/billing/subscription`
(`hard_limit_usd`) plus `{base}/v1/dashboard/billing/usage`
(`total_usage`); remaining = limit − used ($). Aggregator domains differ
per deployment, so this format is explicit-config only.

### Dual-site provider ids (custom id → site mapping)

Some providers run separate international and China sites with different
endpoints, credential references and currencies. The catalog models each
site as its own **provider id**, so configuring the matching key is all it
takes — and an explicit `providers:` entry reusing one of these ids replaces
the catalog row wholesale (same fields, your endpoint/label/currency):

| provider id | Site | Endpoint | Credential ref | Currency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `siliconflow` | SiliconFlow global | `api.siliconflow.com/v1/user/info` | `SILICONFLOW_API_KEY` | `$` |
| `siliconflow-cn` | SiliconFlow China | `api.siliconflow.cn/v1/user/info` | `SILICONFLOW_CN_API_KEY` | `¥` |
| `minimax` | MiniMax Coding global | `www.minimax.io/v1/token_plan/remains` | `MINIMAX_API_KEY` | — (usage %) |
| `minimax-cn` | MiniMax Coding China | `api.minimaxi.com/v1/token_plan/remains` | `MINIMAX_CN_API_KEY` | — (usage %) |
| `zai` | Z.AI GLM Coding global | `api.z.ai/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` | `ZAI_API_KEY` | — (usage %) |
| `zai-coding-cn` | 智谱 GLM Coding China | `open.bigmodel.cn/api/monitor/usage/quota/limit` | `ZAI_CODING_CN_API_KEY` | — (usage %) |

Both sites of one provider can be on the panel at the same time (configure
both keys); `hide: ["siliconflow"]` drops either row individually.

The currency symbol for balance-kind rows comes from the format by default
(`siliconflow-balance` renders ¥) and can be overridden per row: catalog
rows carry `currency` (the global SiliconFlow row sets `$`), a `catalog:`
override may set it, and explicit `providers:` entries accept a `currency`
field (e.g. `"US$"`).

### ChatGPT subscription (Plus/Pro)

ChatGPT subscription usage is **not** API billing — there is no public
balance/usage API. This plugin calls the same internal usage endpoint Codex
uses, with a ChatGPT OAuth token, and shows the **weekly window** (and the
**5-hour window** on Pro) as a used-percentage row. **Two login methods are
supported**, pick whichever you prefer:

> ⚠️ **Experimental.** The endpoint (`chatgpt.com/backend-api/wham/usage`) is
> an undocumented internal API used by the Codex CLI; its response shape may
> change. The plugin only performs read-only queries.

#### Option A: in-plugin login (recommended — no Codex CLI install required)

1. Restart `dsh web` and open the panel **settings** (gear icon) in the
   bottom-right corner;
2. In the "ChatGPT account" section at the top, click **"Log in to ChatGPT"**;
3. The plugin starts an OAuth device-code flow and displays a **one-time code**
   plus the sign-in URL `https://auth.openai.com/codex/device`;
4. Open the URL in your browser, sign in with your ChatGPT Plus/Pro account,
   and enter the code;
5. Once authorized, a "ChatGPT" row appears automatically (no restart). Hover
   to see `plan: plus/pro` and `weekly: N%` (Pro also shows a 5h window).

Tokens are stored in `$DSH_HOME/dsh-quota-panel/chatgpt-auth.json`
(`C:\Users\<you>\.dsh\dsh-quota-panel\` on Windows, file mode 0600). When the
access token expires the plugin refreshes it with the refresh token and writes
it back. Click "Log out" in the same section to delete the local token.

#### Option B: reuse a Codex CLI login

If you have already logged in via the [Codex CLI](https://developers.openai.com/codex/)
(ran `codex` and completed the browser sign-in), the plugin automatically reads
`~/.codex/auth.json` (or `$CODEX_HOME/auth.json`) — **no extra configuration
needed**. With this method, refreshed tokens stay in the plugin process memory
only and are **never written back** to `auth.json` (that file is owned by the
Codex CLI).

When both are present, the **in-plugin login takes precedence**. When neither
exists the ChatGPT row is hidden. If the token is invalidated by a login
elsewhere, the row shows an error — run Option A again, or `codex login`, to
recover.

### Built-in formats

| format | Row kind | Upstream response shape |
|---|---|---|
| `deepseek-balance` | ¥ balance | `{ balance_infos: [{ currency, total_balance, granted_balance, topped_up_balance }] }` |
| `openrouter-credits` | $ balance | `{ data: { total_credits, total_usage } }` |
| `siliconflow-balance` | balance (¥ by default, per-row currency override) | `{ data: { balance, chargeBalance, totalUsage } }` |
| `moonshot-balance` | ¥ balance | `{ data: { total_balance } }` |
| `minimax-remains` | usage % | `{ base_resp, model_remains: [{ model_name, current_interval_total_count, current_interval_usage_count, current_interval_remaining_percent, end_time, current_weekly_total_count, current_weekly_usage_count, weekly_end_time }] }` — coding model row (MiniMax-M\*) preferred; counts are remaining-side (used = total − count); weekly window only when `current_weekly_total_count > 0` |
| `stepfun-accounts` | ¥ balance | `{ balance, total_cash_balance, total_voucher_balance }` |
| `xai-credits` | $ balance | `{ total: { val } }` (cents → dollars) |
| `openai-billing` | $ balance | aggregator `dashboard/billing` endpoints |
| `zhipu-quota` | text | `{ code: 200, data: { limits: [{ remaining, number }] } }` (limits without `remaining` fall back to `percentage`) |
| `opencode-usage` | usage % | `{ usage: { rolling|weekly|monthly: { percent, resetsAt } } }` |
| `zai-coding-quota` | usage % | `{ code: 200, data: { limits: [{ type: TOKENS_LIMIT \| TIME_LIMIT \| CREDIT_LIMIT, unit, number, percentage, currentValue, usage, remaining, nextResetTime }] } }` — semantic mapping (glm-plan-usage2, issue #2): TOKENS_LIMIT `unit=3` → 5h window, `unit=6` → weekly, TIME_LIMIT → MCP monthly lane; unknown units fall back to `nextResetTime` ordering; every window prefers the `percentage` field. Credit/resource-package plans (issue #7) return CREDIT_LIMIT rows instead of token windows: they map onto rolling/weekly by `nextResetTime` order, and the hover title tags them `[CREDIT_LIMIT left remaining/number]` |
| `kimi-coding-usage` | usage % | `{ usage: { limit, used, remaining, resetTime }, limits: [{ window: { duration, timeUnit }, detail: { limit, used, remaining, resetTime } }] }` — 5h = the `duration=300` window, weekly = `duration=10080` (fallback: top-level usage); used = limit − remaining |
| `volcengine-agent-usage` | usage % | Dispatched inline in `fetchRow` (not through `adaptRow`): signs and calls the Volcengine Ark OpenAPI `GetAFPUsage`, parsing `Result.AFPFiveHour / AFPWeekly / AFPMonthly` (Agent Plan 5h/weekly/monthly; AFPDaily skipped per the console). |
| `volcengine-coding-usage` | usage % | Dispatched inline in `fetchRow` (not through `adaptRow`): signs and calls the Volcengine Ark OpenAPI `GetCodingPlanUsage`, parsing `Result.QuotaUsage[].Level ∈ {session,weekly,monthly}` (Coding Plan session/weekly/monthly, percentages only). Independent from the Agent row — no fallback between them. |
| `chatgpt-subscription` | usage % | `{ plan_type, rate_limit: { primary_window: { used_percent, reset_at, limit_window_seconds }, secondary_window? } }` — read via the OAuth token in `~/.codex/auth.json` against Codex's internal usage endpoint; windows are classified by `limit_window_seconds` (18000s ≈ 5h → rolling, 604800s ≈ 7d → weekly), falling back to the typical positional layout (primary = 5h session, secondary = weekly pool). Experimental |

### Proxy (providers that cannot be reached directly)

Configure per-provider proxies in the **frontend settings panel (⚙ →
代理)**: fill an HTTP(S) proxy URL (e.g. `http://127.0.0.1:7890`,
user:pass allowed), saved to browser localStorage, effective immediately —
leave it empty to fall back to the profile config or a direct connection.
Requests still run host-side: the browser sends each row's proxy URL in the
`fetch-all` payload, the host validates it (http/https only, socks
rejected) and fetches through it — keys never reach the browser, but the
proxy itself can observe them (see [Known issues & risks](#known-issues--risks-proxy-path)
under Security).

The profile `proxies` map + row-level `proxy` /
`catalog.<id>.proxy` remain available as **default proxies** (used when
the frontend field is empty). Precedence:
**frontend settings > profile config > direct**.

```yaml
# example profile-level default proxy (the ⚙ panel can override per row)
- id: quota-panel
  name: 'dsh-quota-panel'
  config:
    proxies:
      home: http://127.0.0.1:7890     # local proxy http port (clash / v2rayN …)
    catalog:
      openrouter:
        proxy: home                    # OpenRouter via proxy by default
    providers:
      - id: my-agg
        label: My aggregator
        credential: AGG_API_KEY
        endpoint: https://agg.example  # base URL for openai-billing
        format: openai-billing
        proxy: home
```

### Threshold defaults

DeepSeek balance (`balanceTiers {critical: 10, warn: 20, healthy: 50}`):

| Balance | Status | Secondary info |
|---|---|---|
| `<= 10` | error (red dot + red value) | 建议充值 |
| `10 < x <= 20` | warn (amber) | 余额紧张 |
| `20 < x <= 50` | ok | 余额正常 |
| `> 50` | ok | 余额充足 |

OpenCode usage (`high = max(rolling, weekly, monthly)`):

| Usage | Status |
|---|---|
| `< warnPercent` | ok (green dot, DeepSeek-blue bar) |
| `>= warnPercent` | warn (amber dot + bar) |
| `>= errorPercent` | error (red dot + bar) |

## Install

**Install a released version — not the `main` branch.** `main` receives
unverified work-in-progress; only tagged releases have passed the CI gates
(check + boot) and — for stable versions — the human approval gate.

**Recommended — the latest stable release (or the latest pre-release for the
current iteration cycle):**

```sh
# Pin the latest stable release tag (checked on the Releases page)
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:wenzetan/dsh-quota-panel#v0.8.0"

# Or, once the repo secret NPM_TOKEN is configured (see below), by name —
# npm `latest` always resolves to the last human-approved stable:
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-quota-panel
# Restart `dsh web` (bundle layer and client module graph apply at boot)
```

**When you want the latest pre-release** (e.g. testing the current
`0.8.0-rc.N` iteration):

```sh
# Pin the pre-release tag
dsh plugin --profile web add "github:wenzetan/dsh-quota-panel#v0.8.0-rc.1"
# Or from npm under the `next` dist-tag:
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-quota-panel@next
```

> **Avoid bare `github:wenzetan/dsh-quota-panel`** (no `#tag`) — it tracks
> `main` HEAD, which is the testing branch: it may carry unreleased work,
> fail CI, or break. Only developers iterating on the plugin itself should
> install from `main`.

Refresh the browser page once after installing. Zero npm dependencies (the
schema library — schemastery + cosmokit, both MIT — is vendored under
`src/vendor/` with relative-path imports), no `allowBuilds` authorization
needed.

### Release channels & npm publishing (maintainer)

Versioning policy — the version string picks the channel:

| package.json version | Channel | Gate | GitHub Release | npm dist-tag |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `0.8.0-rc.1` (any `-suffix`) | pre-release | CI only (check + boot) | flagged **pre-release** | `next` |
| `0.8.0` (plain `X.Y.Z`) | stable | CI **+ human approval** | normal release | `latest` |

Workflow:

1. **Iterate (automatic)**

# dsh-session-manager

**Session recycle bin & permanent delete for DeepSeek Harness.**

Move the current session into a recycle bin from the conversation header, restore or permanently delete archived sessions (single or batch), with live-session protection.

The interface automatically follows the browser language: Chinese locales use
Chinese and all other locales use English.

[English](README.md) | [中文](README.zh.md)

---

## ✨ Features

- **Conversation-header archive button** — move the current session into the recycle bin from the header (no confirmation; always recoverable).
- **No duplicate of DSH's own affordance** — archiving from the sidebar uses DSH's built-in hover button; this plugin no longer injects a second, differently worded icon (0.4.4 removed the old row trash icon and the document-wide MutationObserver that drove it).
- **Recycle-bin manager** (Settings → 🗑 会话回收站) — archived sessions with multi-select: batch restore, batch permanent delete; each item shows its ID and path.
- **True permanent delete** — physically removes the session log from disk and the projection-cache record; ghost sessions (records without a log) are cleaned up so they vanish instead of lingering.
- **Live-session protection** — sessions with an active agent are refused deletion.
- **Sub-session aware** — each row can show how many sub-agent sessions it left behind (whole tree, any depth) and open them inline: title, size, time and running state, with a checkbox per sub-session. Permanent delete removes the whole tree; the ones you uncheck are kept and stay reachable as a "deleted main session · N sub-sessions kept" row instead of becoming invisible leftovers.
- **Running sub-agents block the row** — a session is refused while any sub-session in its tree is still running, and the refusal names it.
- **Batch fault tolerance** — batch operations delete per-session with error collection and reporting.
- **Light/dark adaptive UI** — all colors are CSS custom properties in `client.css`; components follow the resolved DSH appearance (`data-ds-dark-theme`) with `prefers-color-scheme` as the OS-level fallback (no hardcoded palette). UI and code text follow the app font too (`--dsw-font-family` / `--ds-font-family-code`), so the Settings → 字体 choice applies here as well.

---

## 📋 Requirements

- **DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 or newer** (this release is tested on that version only; older hosts are untested).

  The recycle-bin list no longer reads session logs: its titles and turn counts come from the Session projection cache (`SessionProjectionCache.cachedSnapshot`, plus `cachedPredecessorTitle` for checkpoints written by an older format generation) — the same zero-I/O face DSH's own session list uses. On a host without those two methods the plugin still mounts, archives and restores, but the list degrades to 「未命名会话」 with no turn counts.

  The floor is declared as `dsh.engines.dsh`. Note that DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 does **not** read that field: it is documentation for users and marketplaces, not a runtime gate.

---

## 📦 Install

### One-click from the plugin market (dsh-market)

Once listed in the [awesome-dsh-plugin](https://awesome-dsh-plugin.com) registry: open **Settings → Plugin Market** → search **dsh-session-manager** → install.

### Manual

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-session-manager
```

Then restart the web app (stop the `dsh web` process and run `dsh web` again).

### Local development install

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web add link:/absolute/path/to/harness-session-delete
```

### Uninstall

```bash
dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-session-manager
```

---

## 🚀 Usage

1. **Move to the recycle bin** — click the 「移入回收站」 icon in the conversation header: the session is archived and an undo toast appears. Whether an archived session keeps showing in the left sidebar is decided by DSH's own **View options → Filter sessions** setting (Hide archived / All conversations / Archived only); this plugin does not touch it, exactly like DSH's built-in archive button.
2. **Settings recycle bin** — open **Settings ⚙️ → 🗑 会话回收站**:
   - Checkbox multi-select → **Restore** (batch unarchive) or **Permanent delete** (batch purge).
   - Each entry shows the session name, ID and working path (hover for full details).
3. **Permanent delete** physically removes the log and projection cache; live sessions are protected.
4. **Undo** — restoring shows an undo toast that re-archives the session.

---

## 🛠 Development

```bash
pnpm test          # run the test suite (host logic + HTTP routes)
```

Repo layout:

```
harness-session-delete/
├── package.json            # single bundle manifest (dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client)
├── cordis.patch.yml        # bundle patch: one insert mounting the host row
├── index.js                # node half: host entry (inject + apply)
├── client.js               # browser half: conversation-header action + settings recycle bin
├── client.css              # plugin stylesheet: design tokens + light/dark adaptive components
└── packages/
    └── session-trash-host/ # host implementation (persistence/workspace/cache patches, HTTP routes)
```

### Changelog convention

`CHANGELOG.md` and `CHANGELOG.zh.md` mirror each other. Every entry follows:

- Version section `## [version] - YYYY-MM-DD`, with only the `### Added` / `### Changed` / `### Fixed` / `### Performance` / `### Removed` headings it actually uses.
- One topic per bullet: **a short bold lead stating the outcome**, then 1-2 sentences on what changed and why it matters.
- No implementation detail, no code, no test or verification results — those belong in the commit or the PR.
- Write only user-visible or breaking changes; skip internal refactors with no visible effect.

---

## 🔌 How it works

- A **single npm bundle** covers both halves, same as other published plugins: the host row mounts via `cordis.patch.yml`; the browser half joins automatically through `dsh.client` + `exports["./client"]`.
- The browser talks to the host over the plugin's own `/api/session-trash/*` HTTP routes (registered on the webserver; non-GET requests carry an `x-dsh-plugin` CSRF header).

---

## 📄 License

[MIT](LICENSE)
