evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# Workspace Copilot An AI-assistant showcase inspired by Copilot-class plugins. It inspects the active repository through a lifecycle-scoped Node backend, identifies languages, frameworks, scripts, and important files, then opens a Composer-adjacent suggestion popover that inserts grounded intents directly into the active draft. Public contracts demonstrated: - `weworkPluginRuntime` - `ctx.wework.backend` - `ctx.wework.chat.providers` - `ctx.wework.commands` - `ctx.wework.composer` - `composer.slash` - `wework.composer.action` The scanner uses breadth-first sampling so a large first package cannot consume the whole scan budget and hide the rest of a monorepo. # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wework DSH 扩展 Demo 这是“Wework 插件开发”Skill 携带的可运行 Core DSH 插件示例，覆盖 Wework 当前公开的全部 UI 扩展点。模型可以复制该目录作为实现参考；桌面应用不会自动启用 它。 先把该目录复制到可写的项目目录，再在 Wework 的“插件 → 管理 → Wework 插件”中 输入复制后目录的绝对路径，例如： ```text file:/absolute/path/to/ui-extension-demo ``` 安装完成后重启 Core DSH。左侧会出现 `DSH Demo`，应用切换器、设置页、Composer、 工作区工具栏、底部面板、新建工作区 Tab 菜单和全局 overlay 也会出现对应示例。 示例还注册了一个可从 Composer、工作区工具栏以及 `Command+Shift+D` （Windows/Linux 为 `Ctrl+Shift+D`）触发的统一命令，并演示上下文条件、配置和 持久化状态。 停用或卸载插件并重启后，所有贡献会随同一 DSH 生命周期一起移除。 关键文件： - `package.json` 声明 DSH bundle、client 依赖和浏览器平台。 - `cordis.patch.yml` 把插件加入 DSH Loader 树。 - `index.js` 是 host 入口；纯 UI 插件可以保持为空。 - `client.js` 通过 `ctx.wework` 注册命令、菜单、快捷键、配置与状态，并通过 `ctx.wework.contributions` 注册宿主描述、通过原生 `ctx.slots.register` 注册自定义 UI。 - 左侧 `DSH Demo` 入口通过公开的 `workspaceTab` 路由参数首次创建独立 Tab， 后续点击复用同一个 Tab，不会覆盖用户当前正在使用的 Tab。 生产插件应更换包名、ID、文案和样式，并只注册实际需要的扩展点。 # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

# Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | # Wegent > An open-source AI work system spanning your local desktop, cloud agents, and remote machines. English | [简体中文](README_zh.md) [![CI](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/actions/workflows/test.yml) [![License](https://img.shields.io/github/license/wecode-ai/Wegent)](LICENSE) [![GitHub Issues](https://img.shields.io/github/issues/wecode-ai/Wegent)](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) Wegent includes a desktop workbench and a self-hostable web platform. Wegent Desktop works with local projects, files, commands, tests, and code changes. Wegent Web provides browser-based agents, knowledge, automation, and administration. Wegent Backend connects these applications to shared project spaces, models, and execution devices. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) · [Documentation](https://wecode-ai.github.io/wegent-docs/) · [Contributing](CONTRIBUTING.md) ## Wegent Desktop Wegent Desktop organizes local coding work by project and task. The task view keeps the conversation, tool activity, tests, changed files, and diffs together; the project-space view provides the board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

Running and reviewing a local coding task in Wegent Desktop.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. [Download the latest Wegent Desktop installer](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/releases/latest) and install it. 2. Open the app and add or select a local project. 3. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. Review the agent activity, command output, and file changes. ### Wegent Web and Backend To start the self-hosted web application and Backend in standalone mode with Docker: ```bash curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --standalone ``` Open http://localhost:3000 and follow the setup flow to create the administrator password and configure a model. See the [Installation Guide](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) and [Standalone Mode](docs/en/wegent/deployment/standalone-mode.md) for other deployment options. ## Development Requires Node.js 20+ and pnpm: ```bash pnpm install pnpm --filter wework dev ``` To run the macOS desktop app: ```bash pnpm --filter wework dev:mac ``` See [wework/README.md](wework/README.md) for desktop development, build, and release instructions. `wework/` is the current desktop application source directory. ## Repository map ### Products and services | Directory | Responsibility | | -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- | | `wework/` | Wegent Desktop (Electron, Vite, React) | | `wework-mobile/` | Independent Expo application for iOS and Android | | `frontend/` | Wegent Web (Next.js, React) | | `backend/` | Default public API, business logic, and data models | | `backend-rs/` | Rust hybrid gateway and APIs that have completed migration | | `executor/` | Rust task executor, local-device runtime, and Codex integration | | `executor_manager/` | Server-side executor scheduling, sandboxes, and orchestration | | `chat_shell/` | Lightweight chat and agent runtime | | `knowledge_runtime/` | Knowledge indexing and retrieval API | | `knowledge_doc_converter/` | Document parsing and asynchronous conversion service | ### Shared code and developer tools | Directory | Responsibility | | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `knowledge_engine/` | Reusable Python kernel for parsing, indexing, vector stores, and retrieval | | `shared/` | Python models, protocols, utilities, and telemetry shared by services | | `packages/` | TypeScript chat and collaboration modules shared by Web and Desktop | | `sdk/` | Plugin authentication, build, creation, and DingTalk workspace SDKs | | `wegent-cli/` | Python CLI for managing Wegent CRD resources | ### Infrastructure, tests, and documentation | Directory | Responsibility | | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | `docker/` | Service images, standalone resources, and the `docker/telemetry/` observability stack | | `scripts/` | Installation, release, acceptance, repository-policy, and development automation | | `tests/` | Cross-service Playwright integration tests and installation tests | | `docs/` | English and Chinese user docs, developer docs, architecture, and historical designs | | `patches/` | Third-party dependency patches used by pnpm `patchedDependencies` | | `LICENSES/` | Third-party license texts required for repository distribution | | `.github/` | CI, release workflows, composite actions, and repository automation | ### Root entry points | File | Responsibility | | -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `start.sh`, `install.sh` | Local startup and self-hosted installation | | `build_image.sh`, `build_image_mac.sh` | Multi-architecture and host Docker image builds | | `docker-compose*.yml` | Default, build, and E2E Compose orchestration | | `package.json`, `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | JavaScript/TypeScript workspace definition | | `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock` | Repository-level Python tooling and lock metadata | | `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md` | Contributor rules and compatibility symlink | ## Documentation - [Wegent Desktop documentation](docs/en/wework/README.md) - [Desktop development and release](wework/README.md) - [Wegent quick start](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/quick-start.md) - [Installation and deployment](docs/en/wegent/getting-started/installation.md) - [Core concepts](docs/en/wegent/concepts/core-concepts.md) - [Developer guide](docs/en/wegent/developer-guide/README.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/en/wegent/troubleshooting.md) ## Contributing Bug reports, documentation improvements, code contributions, and new ways of using Wegent are all welcome. - [Contributing Guide](CONTRIBUTING.md) - [Security Policy](SECURITY.md) - [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/wecode-ai/Wegent/issues) - DingTalk Community: “wework社区交流”, group ID `190890002451` - [Discord Community](https://discord.gg/MVzJzyqEUp) - [License](LICENSE) ## Contributors Thanks to everyone who helps Wegent grow.

A project space in Wegent Desktop with its task board, shared files, automation, and execution status.

## Features - **Desktop workbench** — Organize local projects, tasks, sessions, files, tool activity, tests, and diffs. - **Reusable agents** — Combine models, prompts, Skills, knowledge, tools, and collaboration settings. - **Project spaces** — Share task boards, files, discussions, automation, execution history, and deliveries. - **Multiple execution targets** — Run tasks locally, on remote work machines, or with server-managed executors. - **Self-hosting** — Deploy Wegent Web and Backend for team access, APIs, permissions, scheduling, and knowledge services. ## Why Wegent **The local coding experience built on Codex is the foundation of Wegent Desktop.** It works directly with the code, files, commands, and development environment in your projects. Connect it to Wegent Backend when coding work needs to move beyond one computer or one person. Once connected, the desktop workbench and Web use the same projects, tasks, and execution devices. - **Run tasks on the right device** — Keep using the code, files, commands, and development environment already on a local machine, or run a task for the same project on a remote work machine or server-managed executor. - **Move a project forward as a team** — Project spaces connect task boards, shared files, discussions, execution status, and deliveries instead of leaving conversations and code changes on separate computers. - **Automate repeated project work** — Project spaces can configure automation and execution queues to keep routine work moving. - **Keep services and data under team control** — Self-host Web and Backend for shared access, permissions, model configuration, scheduling, knowledge services, and remote-device management. If work always stays on one computer, Wegent Desktop provides a familiar Codex coding experience. Connect it to Wegent to extend that experience when tasks must move across people, devices, or a self-hosted environment. ## Wegent Web Wegent Web provides the browser interface for remote agents. Agents can use configured models, knowledge, Skills, and tools while Wegent Backend manages their tasks and execution.

A Wegent remote agent uses tools to generate a Gantt chart.

## How it works Wework is the Wegent desktop workbench. Electron owns desktop windows, system capabilities, and process management. DeepSeek Harness (DSH) is the embedded application and plugin runtime, and the Wework product UI is composed from a set of DSH plugins. Executor manages tasks and sessions, then drives Codex to perform the actual work in local projects. ```mermaid flowchart LR Electron["Electron
Desktop host"] subgraph DSH["DSH Runtime"] direction TB Core["DSH Core
Plugin discovery, dependency injection, and lifecycle"] App["dsh-app-wework
Wework product shell and UI extension points"] UI["dsh-ui-*
Tasks, project spaces, settings, apps, and automation"] ElectronPlugin["dsh-electron-host
Electron capability bridge"] ExecutorPlugin["dsh-executor-runtime
Task execution and event adapter"] TerminalPlugin["dsh-terminal-runtime
Local interactive terminals"] Core --> App Core --> UI Core --> ElectronPlugin Core --> ExecutorPlugin Core --> TerminalPlugin App --> UI end Executor["Executor
Task and session execution"] Codex["Codex
Coding agent"] Workspace["Local project
Files and commands"] Electron -->|"Starts and hosts"| Core Electron -->|"Starts and supervises"| Executor ElectronPlugin <-->|"Restricted desktop capabilities"| Electron UI <-->|"User actions and UI updates"| ExecutorPlugin ExecutorPlugin -->|"Create, follow up, approve, cancel"| Executor Executor -->|"Status, messages, tool events, results"| ExecutorPlugin Executor <-->|"Launch, control, and events"| Codex Codex <-->|"Read, modify, and execute"| Workspace TerminalPlugin <-->|"PTY"| Workspace ``` DSH does not execute coding tasks itself. `dsh-app-wework` defines the product shell and extension points, `dsh-ui-*` provides the product modules, `dsh-electron-host` bridges restricted Electron capabilities, `dsh-executor-runtime` communicates bidirectionally with Executor throughout execution, and `dsh-terminal-runtime` manages local interactive terminals. Executor is the task execution layer, while Codex is the concrete coding agent it drives. Wework can also connect to Wegent Backend for shared project spaces, models, and remote execution devices. Wegent Web is a separate browser interface built on the same Backend. ## Quick start ### Wegent Desktop 1. Create a task and describe the work to perform. 4. evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# dsh-brand-custom

Replace the four places DeepSeek Harness paints its own brand — the sidebar's
mark and wordmark, and the new-session page's mark and headline — from a
**Settings → Brand** page (in Chinese: 设置 → 品牌自定义).

Everything is optional. A field you leave empty keeps the official artwork or
copy, so an untouched install behaves exactly like a stock one.

| Slot | Default | What you can set |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Sidebar mark | the DeepSeek fish | PNG / JPEG / WebP / SVG, up to 4 MB |
| Sidebar wordmark | `deepseek` + `HARNESS` badge | two independent labels |
| New-session mark | the animated hero fish | PNG / JPEG / WebP / SVG, up to 4 MB |
| New-session headline | `探索未至之境` (localized) | headline and its preview badge |

中文说明见 [README.zh-CN.md](README.zh-CN.md)。

## Install

```sh
dsh plugin --profile <name> add github:what-is-me/dsh-brand-custom
```

`<name>` is the profile you run, for example `desktop`. The argument is the
repository URL, not a path: the plugin manager recognises a hosted repository
URL as a git spec, checks the GitHub connection anonymously before pnpm starts,
and records the dependency as `github:what-is-me/dsh-brand-custom` in the
profile manifest.

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so the same command that installs it
also appends `dsh-brand-custom` to the profile's bundle list — no manual
`cordis.patch.yml` edit. Restart the app (or reload the page after a client
rebuild) and the section appears in Settings.

Pin a revision or tag by appending it: `…dsh-brand-custom#v0.1.0`.

To remove it: `dsh plugin --profile <name> remove dsh-brand-custom`, then drop
`dsh-brand-custom` from `dsh.profile.bundles` if it is still listed.

Working from a local checkout instead? `dsh plugin --profile <name> add
link:/absolute/path/to/dsh-brand-custom` installs the same package without a
clone, and is what you want while editing it.

## How the four slots are taken over

The host paints its brand through three single slots and one hard-coded line:

- `sidebar.brand.mark` — the rail and expanded-header fish, `{ size: 24 }`.
- `sidebar.brand.name` — the wordmark text, no owner props.
- `conversation.hero.brand.mark` — the hero fish, `{ size: 34, className }`.
- The hero headline has **no slot**: the host renders it from its own locale
  dictionary into a span inside the `Hqq-bq_titleGroup` frame.

The plugin therefore does two different things:

1. **Slots.** `@deepseek-ai/dsh-client-ui-brand-official` occupies the first
   three at the default priority (0). This plugin registers at **priority -1**,
   which the slot service resolves as "lowest renders", so the registration
   shadows the official occupant while it exists. The registration lives only
   while the reader has supplied that value: clearing a field disposes it and
   the official brand comes straight back — no repaint logic needed.
2. **Headline text.** The span is rewritten on the DOM, with the host's own
   text captured before the first write so clearing the field restores it. A
   `MutationObserver` keeps it rewritten across language switches and hero
   remounts, and disconnects entirely once nothing is customized. The frame is
   found through the mark slot's own outlet
   (`[data-slot="conversation.hero.brand.mark"]`), so no hashed class name is
   ever written down here.

## Storage

The node half owns everything; the browser half only reads it back.

```
$DSH_HOME/plugins/dsh-brand-custom/
  config.json          # { version: 1, text: { four nullable slots } }
  sidebar-mark.<ext>   # exactly one of png/jpg/webp/svg, or absent
  hero-mark.<ext>
```

Images are written through a temporary file and a rename, then any other
extension of the same kind is removed, so a status read always sees one file.
Uploads are checked against the declared content type (PNG and WebP signature
bytes; SVG is text) and capped at 4 MB.

## HTTP surface

| Method | Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `GET` | `/brand-custom-api/config` | `{ ok, text, images }` |
| `PUT` | `/brand-custom-api/config` | merge `{ text }`, answer the new state |
| `GET`/`HEAD` | `/brand-custom-api/image/<kind>` | the stored bytes |
| `PUT` | `/brand-custom-api/image/<kind>` | replace (content-type names the format) |
| `DELETE` | `/brand-custom-api/image/<kind>` | remove |

`kind` is `sidebar-mark` or `hero-mark`. Every route is fenced to loopback
clients with a loopback `Host` header, a same-origin `Sec-Fetch-Site`, and an
`Origin` that matches the host; the images are served with `nosniff` and a
`default-src 'none'` CSP because an SVG is a document that can carry script.

## Failure containment

A plugin must not be able to take the app down with it, so both halves refuse
to let their own failures escape.

The web boot is the strict one: after the client entries settle it walks every
entry and throws `web boot: N entries did not activate …` for **any** entry that
is not `active` — a plugin whose `apply` throws leaves the whole page on its
loading screen (`bZ` in the web frontend bundle). The node half is more
forgiving: only entries on the global required list reject startup, and a normal
bundle that fails becomes `warning: N entries did not activate` with its
siblings still running.

So the browser half wraps every step whose failure is survivable in `safely()`
and logs `dsh-brand-custom: <step> unavailable — <message>` instead of throwing:
locale registration and binding, the headline observer, the initial state read,
the settings section, and each of the three slot takeovers. A host that drops
`settings.section` or already holds the locale namespace costs the reader that
one feature and nothing else.

The node half contains failures the same way: route bodies run through `guard()`
so a throw answers `500 {"ok":false,"error":"internal error"}` instead of
surfacing as an unhandled rejection, a refused route registration is logged and
skipped rather than thrown out of `apply`, and `readBody` settles on `close` as
well as `end`/`error` so a client that disconnects mid-upload cannot leave the
handler pending.

## Tests

```sh
node test/smoke.mjs        # node half: all routes, fence, signatures, storage
node test/client-smoke.mjs # browser half: registration shapes against stubs
node test/takeover.mjs     # slot takeover: occupied only while a value exists
node test/hero-text.mjs    # headline rewrite and its restore-on-clear
node test/hardening.mjs    # failure containment: broken services cost one feature
```

The browser-half tests run without a DOM or `react-dom`: they call the plugin's
components as plain functions with `useSyncExternalStore` stubbed to the live
snapshot, and build a hand-made element tree for the headline rewrite.

## Known limits

- The hero headline rewrite depends on the hero frame's structure (mark outlet
  inside the hitbox, title group beside it). If a future build changes that
  frame, the rewrite silently stops applying — the slots keep working.
- The sidebar wordmark is the host's own two-part layout re-created by hand, so
  a host restyle will not propagate to it while a label is customized.
